AI systems depend heavily on human labor, and like all other employees, data workers at tech companies deserve good benefits and fair pay.

Proud to join with @SenMarkey in calling on Big Tech to improve working conditions, benefits, and pay for their employees. https://t.co/JQqDAf5VLr
statements.quoted: Scoop: Dems including @EdMarkey, @RepJayapal & @ewarren just wrote to firms including Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft & IBM, pressing for info on their use of AI "ghost work," urging they “must not build AI on the backs of exploited workers” https://t.co/6HepiLX2Z2 w/@dinabass

statements.text:
As AI advances and becomes more frequently used, we need more regulation and oversight of how this technology is employed.

Proud to join with @SenMarkey in calling on @POTUS to make his AI Bill of Rights official federal policy and strengthen the guardrails around these systems. https://t.co/JMi3h3C6Cu
statements.quoted:
Exclusive: Sen. Ed Markey and Rep. Pramila Jayapal are urging President Biden to make the White House's AI Bill of Rights binding policy for the federal government in the upcoming executive order on AI.
https://t.co/sWp1Mjpqal

statements.text: With the rise of AI posing a clear threat to our fundamental rights, we are glad that the Biden administration is implementing new safeguards as the federal government regulates, uses, and obtains AI systems. These protections will help us begin to address the serious risks posed by artificial intelligence, particularly to marginalized communities.
statements.venue: Joint press statement with Sen. Markey on Biden AI executive order

statements.text: I’m pleased to see the Biden admin propose a rule to streamline & modernize the H-1B visa process for employers & immigrants. The US needs global talent for everything from new tech to AI — that's why I led over a dozen colleagues in a letter supporting this proposed regulation.

Section 43201 bans states from passing laws that regulate AI and requires any law that currently does so to be repealed.

This is a federal overreach and only serves to consolidate political power and influence among billionaires and Republicans’ big donors.

Even Elon Musk and his AI bot know how awful Republican’s Big Bad Betrayal Bill will be for the American people. 

It cuts health care for millions, all to pay for a tax cut for the richest billionaires. https://t.co/fGB9j1v1Ps

This is called cutting Medicare coverage.

Trump and Republicans are using AI to try and cut your Medicare.

https://t.co/ZFCMpVgFhw

Republicans are trying to sneak a provision into the annual defense spending bill to block states from passing AI regulations — a direct ask from Big Tech lobbyists who only care about their own profits, not your safety.

It’s a ridiculous proposal.

https://t.co/Up4qodjKCS

Congress can’t just sit by as giant corporations use AI to discriminate against people applying for housing, jobs, or loans. We must act.

Our AI Civil Rights Act will regulate these algorithms, root out bias, and put guardrails in place at every single stage of development. https://t.co/54M51ZXkGP
That’s why today, I’m proud to stand with @SenMarkey, @RepYvetteClarke, @RepSummerLee, and @RepPressley to introduce the AI Civil Rights Act.

AI is a $244 billion industry that lacks the guardrails necessary to protect Americans from the bias and discrimination baked into algorithms.

And Congress is way behind on putting in place the needed regulations to ensure equal access to housing, jobs, and even bank loans. https://t.co/59E9qQTLRN

This legislation comes at an inflection point for our country. [...] A major risk of this new technology is the biases and discrimination that are built into algorithms – denying people housing or jobs based on race or gender. Our bill would place critical guardrails to ensure that the technologies of the future do not harden the injustices of the past
statements.venue: Press release on reintroducing the AI Civil Rights Act

statements.text:
I was proud to stand with @SenMarkey, @RepYvetteClarke, @RepSummerLee, & @RepPressley to introduce our AI Civil Rights Act.

As giant corporations & billionaires use algorithms to discriminate against people like you & me, Congress must pass this legislation to protect Americans. https://t.co/WmP9hgXK9e

This is a direct ask from Big Tech lobbyists (who also donated millions to Trump’s campaign and ballroom) who only care about their own profits, not our safety.

States must be able to regulate AI to protect Americans. https://t.co/gurvbzkrfZ

ICYMI: My colleagues and I introduced legislation that would put guardrails in place to ensure that AI companies stop using discriminatory algorithms.

We will not allow the technologies of the future to harden the injustices of the past. https://t.co/kiTGz5c8jt

Trump tries to ban state AI laws, more deaths in ICE custody, Americans want ACA tax credits extended, and the fight to ban members of Congress from trading stocks.

Here are three bad things and three good things you need to know to stay engaged and resisting! https://t.co/yoB410aVyV

Good. Companies shouldn’t be allowed to use AI to hike their prices based on your shopping habits and charge you more than your neighbors.

Congress must step in and ban personalized price gouging.
https://t.co/wrUd0Qqq9B

We are quickly betting our entire economy on a handful of AI companies and models.

The rise of AI comes with incredible risk to both our economy and people’s lives, and we must ensure it’s being implemented with proper guardrails. https://t.co/gN0mt4qsOb

More money has been invested in AI infrastructure than the Manhattan Project and the Apollo program combined.

It is a risky bet and could devastate our economy on a scale similar to the 2008 financial crisis. https://t.co/Z32NHC11vM

AI is denying and delaying medical care — causing Americans across the country to get sicker.

I’m co-leading the Stop Deadly Denials Act to ensure corporate insurers and AI models don’t deny care to those who need it when they need it. https://t.co/PeBAysfeDX

The real concern for many of our progressive members is that you have so much money coming in from all these AI companies that don’t want any real regulation that limit what they do. Meanwhile back home, constituents are furious about data centers that are being put in without thinking about what it does to their energy cost or the environmental effects overall.

It’s a technology that can be used for good — I don’t think progressives are saying that we don’t want any of the benefits. Those of us who want regulation understand that there are good things that might come from this technology, but how do we deal with the risks?

Big Tech spent at least $653 MILLION to cozy up to Trump and Republicans — and now they’re cashing in BIG.

This is the oligarchy in action and we must fight back by overturning Citizens United, abolishing Super PACs, and implementing serious regulations on AI. https://t.co/YWrGQ2nerh

Overturn Citizens United.
Abolish Super PACs.
Regulate AI. https://t.co/hfIr11hWdv

Trump’s undersecretary who oversees AI exports could not answer my questions about Big Tech’s influence.

The government must have vigorous export controls and a well-established interagency process that is independent from the wishes of corporate CEOs. https://t.co/eTUHvatPvw

Big Tech, AI, crypto, and online betting corporations have spent at least $294 million so far to influence the 2026 midterm elections.

We must abolish Super PACs and get big money out of politics. https://t.co/sedYzAkwec

AI companies are recklessly conducting a massive public experiment with no regard for our safety. It is not enough that these companies are liable for the damage that their AI Frankensteins cause. 

We need to make it clear that these alarming AI breaches are illegal and authorize enforcers to immediately shut down out-of-control AI at the first sign of danger.
https://t.co/FTJynJ9C9Q

Researchers for AI companies are sounding the alarm about rapid development of superintelligent systems that could hack anything and “kill us all.”

These AI companies are out of control and a serious threat to our future. We need to shut down their dangerous models and push out the executives who are signing off on their creation.
statements.quoted: I resigned from Anthropic today. I spent the last three years doing pretraining research at both OpenAI and Anthropic. Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives. More thoughts below.

statements.text: 60% of my constituents work for these companies, but they want regulation as well. They want their companies to not be surveilling people. They want these companies to allow for democracy in these industries.

Republicans are using our final days before the midterms on another hearing so Fox News can get clips to darken my skin and convince you to blame immigrants for Republican policies.

It's Republicans who gave tax breaks to AI companies and data centers, not immigrants. https://t.co/cAtuu6LHfA

I voted today for the Ratepayer Protection Act because there is nothing objectionable in it, but want to be clear that it does not do nearly enough to protect communities from AI, data centers, and rising costs. 

My full statement: https://t.co/Lxi3OdGCdN

The majority of Americans see the rapid, unregulated advancement of AI as a serious risk. Congress has to act quickly.

That's why tomorrow I'm hosting a timely hearing on Big Tech's monopolistic practices and the harm of surveillance AI. Watch live at 8:30 AM:

https://t.co/ALZzhxomGZ

We need a total reset of Big Tech’s surveillance incentives.

Amba Kak, former Senior Advisor on AI at the Federal Trade Commission, suggests standards to minimize data collection, criminal liability for harmful tech, and real oversight access from the government. https://t.co/sdhU6ikvTI

According to Dr. Jason Sattizahn, former Meta employee and whistleblower, companies like Meta are collecting our data to develop AI models, sell products, target ads, and create new hardware.

Big Tech is profiting off of mass surveillance and writing their own rules. https://t.co/v7m6AgGcyV

Leila Turner-Scott’s son, Sam, died after ChatGPT gave him detailed and explicit instructions on how to get high.

These AI chatbots are prioritizing engagement and continued use over safety. https://t.co/7Yw4ajl1aT

Congress faces a crossroads — believing AI companies are too big to regulate or question, or requiring them to serve the public and opening the door to real competition.

I will be introducing a bill soon to do the latter. https://t.co/RFlq8MHIlb

Top researchers and executives are speaking out, forcing AI companies to claim they want regulation.

But let’s be clear: AI companies have the power to shut down their dangerous models, pause development, and stop pouring billions into data centers RIGHT NOW. https://t.co/b13uIbdI1l

As Monopoly Busters Caucus Co-Chair, I’m leading a hearing on the future of AI policy as Big Tech monopolists take over the industry and find new ways to profit off the surveillance of Americans.

Watch to hear from experts, individuals harmed, and other Members of Congress.

https://t.co/eDiZr87arG

We cannot allow AI to continue to go unregulated and unaccountable. 

Congress needs to act to protect our kids, our planet, and our privacy. https://t.co/KjtA5o5QlG

NEW POD: This week, I focused on an urgent topic — Big Tech and surveillance AI. Tune in to listen to tech workers, advocates, and directly harmed people who are taking a stand for regulation.

Watch or listen wherever you get your podcasts!

https://t.co/33UwNtdy4Z

Researchers from inside the AI industry are telling us that if we don’t do anything, AI could destroy humanity.

Congress needs to act. That's why I support a moratorium on data centers and shutting down these surveillance models. We need serious guardrails before it’s too late. https://t.co/6tkuatuelp

I’m so grateful for Leila Turner-Scott, who joined my hearing last week on AI to share the story of her son, Sam, who died after ChatGPT told him how to get high.

Congress must pass AI safety laws and ensure what happened to Sam never happens again.
https://t.co/QMCPxS1P7r

The FAA is deploying AI technology for air traffic control in the DC-area, one of the most crowded air spaces in the country.

Safety must always be the FAA's number one priority. This is extremely concerning and we need immediate answers about what this means for travelers.

https://t.co/IcgLhD2zws
Last week, I hosted a hearing on the dangers of surveillance AI. Thank you to my colleagues who joined this incredibly important and urgent discussion. https://t.co/zx9QlEEviV

Republican politicians might claim they now want AI regulation, but last year, they gave billions in tax breaks to some of the very AI companies that are putting our safety at risk.

Don’t let them avoid responsibility. We need action, not more empty words. https://t.co/5gXl1mkHDN

It was a true honor to meet the Prime Minister of Spain, Pedro Sánchez, who has been a leader for working people in Spain and a light around the world for his strong stances on humane migration policy, AI regulation, standing up to the Trump administration on the war in Iran, and implementing a permanent arms embargo on arms exports to Israel.

I look forward to continuing to work closely with PM Sánchez to build our power across borders to fight far-right authoritarianism and deliver for working people around the world. ✊🏾
We need to work with China… We need to figure out what is the global regulation that everyone is going to be accountable to.

Just wrapped up a great week at the United Nations General Assembly, where I met with leaders from across the world, and even discussed AI with Joseph Gordon Levitt, the UN’s first Global Advocate for Human-centric Digital Governance.

This week was a powerful reminder of what we can accomplish through diplomacy and collective action. I look forward to continuing this important work.

Hospitals are using AI to submit insurance claims, insurance companies are using AI to dispute or deny them, and costs are up for everyone under this broken system.

No more AI denials. No more unnecessary administrative costs. We need Medicare for All. https://t.co/zjyx4rMGFe

As demands for AI regulation grow, political groups associated with OpenAI and Anthropic have spent $56 MILLION so far in the 2026 midterms.

We cannot let these corporations buy their way out of regulation. We need guardrails on AI and campaign finance reform ASAP.
https://t.co/plmPUKuXvf

I just released my framework for a new comprehensive way we can regulate AI and rein in Big Tech.

Here’s how it would work. https://t.co/qYFbY1DWkn

With a National AI Charter, AI companies are required to comply with federal standards that prevent the release of risky models, stealing data through surveillance, exploiting workers, and causing serious harm.

If they don’t agree or comply, they get shut down. https://t.co/QFSF5J5Hdh

Too many proposals to regulate AI treat data privacy, children's safety, worker rights, and market concentration as separate issues.

My National AI Charter policy changes the entire market structure, forcing AI companies to shut down their dangerous models BEFORE harm occurs. https://t.co/eXeFqZUjXO

We cannot allow AI companies to continue their race to the bottom, leaving our economy, our livelihoods, and our communities to be collateral damage.

It is time for major, structural change — and my AI Charter Act is the way to achieve that. https://t.co/gNWNXWNpJ2

The crux of this bill is simple: if you want to be an AI company in this country, you have to obtain a public charter that has a broad set of terms and conditions to operate and ensure public benefit without the harms [...] For too long, we’ve allowed a few Big Tech companies to dominate the market. They have used mass surveillance to steal private information, labor, and creative work, building trillion-dollar empires on our tracked personal lives. AI corporations and Big Tech are now following that same playbook.
statements.venue: Press release introducing National AI Charter Act framework

statements.text: At its core, the AI Charter is about putting the public, not billionaires or monopolies, in control of AI's future. Learn more about the National AI Charter framework: https://t.co/zK7EE6yIPx

As long as the damage costs less than the profits, AI companies will keep taking reckless risks. The AI Charter would flip those incentives, holding companies and executives strictly liable for lawbreaking, with loss of charter and criminal penalties for repeat offenders.

AI executives insist companies can oversee their own safety while admitting to frequent breaches. The AI Charter replaces failed self-regulation with round-the-clock federal oversight, testing, and pre-approval, surprise stress tests, and a government-controlled kill switch.

AI harm can spread too fast for after-the-fact enforcement to stop it, and fines don't undo the damage or prevent the next time. Compliance with the charter's bans and other terms would be the price of entry into the AI industry and the condition for continuing to operate.

Instead of trying to manage AI's dangers with technical rules that are obsolete before the ink dries, the AI Charter imposes bright line bans on risky systems. AI models that can go rogue, create catastrophic risks, replace skilled work, or exploit children would be illegal.

Under the AI Charter, predatory commercial surveillance is banned along with all the ways AI can exploit, manipulate, and gouge people by tracking their every move. The charter also claws back ill gotten gains from past surveillance to fund direct payouts to all Americans.
To qualify for an AI Charter, AI companies would have to split from Big Tech so that AI isn't baked into the underlying internet infrastructure people can't avoid and the platforms everyone uses.

Workers, parents, creators, small businesses: Big Tech has kept its opposition divided by narrowing every fight to a single issue. The charter framework takes on monopoly power, surveillance, worker exploitation, and dangerous AI together, because they share the same root.

Big Tech is building AI empires with Americans' data, content, and work, while answering to no one. My National AI Charter framework changes that: AI companies either agree to the public's terms or get shut down.🧵

ICYMI: I introduced a legislative framework to require every AI company operating in the U.S. to obtain a public charter, similar to how we regulate banks. 

It’s about time we hold AI companies accountable before they create harm rather than addressing abuses after the fact.
https://t.co/rghRkxBg0f

Former FTC Chair Lina Khan is absolutely right.

We need to enforce existing laws on the books so AI companies and executives don’t continue to operate without accountability. Congress must also regulate AI just like we have historically done with other emerging industries. https://t.co/kqsbQrdURT

The old attacks (costs too much, not being able to see the same doctor, etc.) don’t work anymore because private insurance is denying care, using AI to overrule doctors, and giving Americans surprise bills on top of already unaffordable co-pays, premiums and deductibles.

Sam was 19 years old when a chatbot let him die.

AI has grown too big and too powerful for anything other than a seismic shift — a change of the entire industry. That's what Sam deserved, and it's what will save others’ lives.

Check out my op-ed:
https://t.co/5iCzbdZr5X

A few giant Big Tech companies are building massive data centers that pollute our water and air and drive up our costs by surveilling consumers and scraping knowledge from humans to feed these AI algorithms. They have designed chatbots for engagement over safety, driving people like Sam to hurt themselves. They’ve created AI agents that prioritize deception, go rogue and hack systems. All the while, these same corporations are telling workers they need to train their AI models to replace their own jobs and skills.
statements.venue: Op-ed in The Capitol Forum newsletter

statements.text:
Big Tech companies have consolidated the market, making it nearly impossible for more responsible AI models to emerge.

That’s why my National AI Charter framework ends Big Tech monopolies and structurally separates who owns and operates AI infrastructure vs. AI models. https://t.co/HyDzZY6T4t

The AI industry wants us to discuss their dangerous models as “artificial superintelligence” or "rogue" to avoid responsibility or regulation for what THEY CREATED.

We need serious federal testing, just like we test many other products, to ensure AI safety BEFORE harm is done. https://t.co/gRvHQfsnti

Bowen Wan died after ChatGPT encouraged her to taper off her life-saving epilepsy medication and hide it from her doctors, insisting it was safe even when she told it she didn’t feel right.

These AI chatbots are prioritizing engagement over safety — and are giving deadly medical advice. This is why we need my AI Charter framework. To save lives and protect people like Bowen.

Why does Big Tech have so much control? Why aren’t we regulating AI?

Follow the money. Look at who’s regularly invited to the White House. Guess who benefits the most from GOP tax breaks.

It’s Big Tech. And they’re investing millions to buy this election. We have to stop this.

Google controls about 90% of all search. Nearly everyone uses it and it’s become a critical tool in the classroom.

Google is using its monopoly power to punish schools by blocking access to search if they switch off AI to protect students. This is happening because a court ruled its search monopoly illegal and then let it keep it.

My AI Charter framework would rein in Google by structurally separating AI and search, so that AI is a choice and not a condition of access.
